works.title: dan
works.critique:
The composition employs a tight, cropped close-up on a face, filling the sheet from edge to edge and allowing the spiraled page perforations on the left to frame the boundary. Shading on the bridge of the nose and the orbital sockets relies on continuous, smudged tonal transitions rather than strict contour lines, giving the skin a soft, diffused quality.

The asymmetry between the eyes—one set slightly higher and angled outward—creates a subtle, questioning gaze directed toward the upper right. The title "dan" appears provisionally derived from the file moniker, functioning as a generic identifier rather than an explicit thematic statement.

works.title: assembly
works.description:
CAST & WORLD INDEX
Characters: arc, bolt, flame, jet, madame scarlet, marine, sparrow, vacuum, weapon, wing
Items: Bo Staff, Caped Bodysuit, Fedora, Goggles, Half-Mask, Hooded Cloak, Overcoat, Trenchcoat
Special abilities: Electrical Energy Projection, fire control, Flight / Aerial Leaping, gas control, invisibility, water control
works.critique:
The piece presents a stylized team ensemble featuring ten distinct superheroic/vigilante character archetypes arranged in a layered pyramidal hierarchy. The provisional title "assembly" aptly defines both the narrative trope—a superhero collective gathering—and the formal artistic challenge of grouping disparate anatomical figures into a cohesive tableau.

Compositionally, the central vertical axis is anchored by three tiered figures: a crouching detective archetype in a fedora at the base, a central hooded civilian/leader figure with striking pink hair highlights, and an airborne dynamic figure leaping at the apex. Flanking figures showcase strong silhouette diversity, ranging from high-collared trenchcoat wielders to sleek bodysuit heroines and robotic/armored sentinels. 

The ink treatment relies on confident contour lines and uniform cross-hatching to ground the team on a shared shadow plane. Deliberate red spot-color accents—applied to chest emblems, hair strands, goggles, and the monogram artist signature "JTL"—create a cohesive visual rhythm that leads the viewer's eye across the lineup.

works.title: batman in the belfrey
works.critique:
The piece is an exemplary exercise in tonal restraint and subtractive value rendering. Working with white medium on a pitch-black surface, McGary rejects unnecessary line contour in favor of pure luminosity and negative space. The title "batmaninthebelfrey" functions as a thematic and tonal frame, evoking gothic roosting spaces, elevated solitude, and the quiet vigilance associated with bell towers.

Anatomically and compositionally, the figure emerges from absolute darkness through high-key highlights defining the brow, nose bridge, cowl horns, and upper trapezius. The sweeping cape forms a dominant triangular mass anchored by vertical folds of light that cascade downward to a pool of reflected illumination at the figure's feet. The bat emblem, rendered as an incisive crescent clasp at the collarbone, acts as the central compositional anchor. The economy of mark-making—leaving the entire torso in unbroken shadow—heightens the illusion of monolithic scale and psychological dread.

works.title: Assembly Books 1–3
works.critique:
The manuscript comprises a 23-page compiled sequential arc divided across three distinct episodic installments: *Descent* (Book I), *Into the Mouth of Madness* (Book II), and *Where Hope Shines* (Book III). The overarching narrative explores high-stakes factional warfare, civil unrest, and metahuman accountability across Oceanview.

Compositionally, the pages utilize stark, high-contrast ink linework accented with strategic magenta spot coloring to isolate HUD visors, key energy fields, vehicles, and pivotal character details. Panel architecture moves fluidly between rigid multi-tier gutters and dynamic diagonal framing, using cutaway character portraits and kinetic motion trails to maintain tight pacing. The thematic focus dissects institutional corruption, vigilantism, and moral hypocrisy as federal authorities, local police, the Society of Order and Law (S.O.A.L.), and the emergent Assembly clash over jurisdiction and civilian safety. Character rendering prioritizes strong gestural poses and expressive facial acting, effectively carrying dramatic tension even where secondary background detail is kept minimalist.

works.title: FLAME
works.description:
CAST & WORLD INDEX
Characters: flame
Items: Full-Length Trenchcoat, Half-Mask Visor, High-Collar Bodysuit
Special abilities: Energy Projection / Pyrokinesis, fire manipulation
works.critique:
The drawing functions as a definitive sequential character concept pin-up, utilizing high-contrast black-and-white ink work punctuated by deliberate red accents at the chest harness and collar insignia. The provisional title "IMG_2020_10_21_10_05_56R" indicates an archival camera capture rather than an authored narrative title, shifting critical attention entirely to the visual iconography of the figure itself. 

From a sequential storytelling perspective, the figure's silhouette is immediately legible: the exaggerated bell-sleeves, wide cuffs with high-contrast horizontal banding, and sweeping hemline establish an imposing, grounded center of gravity. The partial face mask—obscuring the right facial plane in stark black shadow while leaving the left eye and cropped hair exposed—conveys an unsettling dualism, suggesting covert identity or technological alteration. Energy or flame wisps rendered with loose, spontaneous contour lines emanate from both lowered hands, framing the lower third of the composition and implying imminent kinetic action or transformation. The controlled use of selective spot color in the red square fasteners and small chest typography anchors the eye at the upper torso, demonstrating deliberate focal hierarchy and visual restraint.

works.title: assembly crayon
works.description:
CAST & WORLD INDEX
Characters: Flame, Jet, Marine, vacuum, Weapon, White Knight
Items: Blonde Visor / Goggles, Green Goblin Mask / Red Suit, Half-Dome Robot Helm, Red Domino / Coat, White Faceless Mask
Places: Oceanview
Special abilities: Energy Manifestation
works.critique:
The composition organizes a multi-character ensemble along a compressed horizontal plane, employing overlapping layers to establish narrative relationships and distinct character heights. Bold, graphic inking defines the contours, anchoring the bright primary hues and waxy crayon textures within structured boundaries. The juxtaposition of disparate visual motifs—from the sharp, red-suited goblin figure in the foreground to the sleek robotic helmet and the relaxed, peace-sign gesture in the midground—generates playful thematic friction across the lineup.

The provisional title "assembly crayon" succinctly identifies the medium and the formal gathering of the squad. The anatomical draftsmanship is stylized and expressive, emphasizing attitude, stance, and costume geometry over strict naturalism.

works.title: SPARROW
works.description:
CAST & WORLD INDEX
Characters: Sparrow
Items: Armored Bodysuit, Full-Face Mask, Side Holster/Baton/escrima sticks, Strapped Greaves
Special abilities: bow, escrima, martial arts
works.critique:
The drawing establishes a clear, centered vertical hierarchy focused entirely on character anatomy and tactical silhouette. The figure is posed in a rigid frontal stance, allowing the detailed linear architecture of the armored suit, articulated knee guards, and symmetrical strap system to read clearly. Form and volume are communicated through disciplined directional hatching and density modulation rather than heavy tonal fills.

The piece gains substantial visual tension through the juxtaposition of the severe, faceless angular mask with the youthful silhouette of pigtails protruding from the sides. The explicit authored title "SPARROW" operates in direct contrast with the heavy, restrained nature of the armor: rather than evoking an agile, lightweight bird in flight, the character is visually anchored, encased, and bound by utilitarian hardware.

works.title: roadhouse poster
works.critique:
The piece is a hand-drawn key-art poster study paying tribute to the 1989 action cult classic *Road House*. The provisional title "roadhouse poster" directly identifies its structural and commercial function as an illustrated theatrical one-sheet. 

McGary constructs a tri-tiered compositional hierarchy typical of classic hand-rendered cinematic posters. The foreground right is dominated by a three-quarter bust portrait of Patrick Swayze as the philosophical cooler James Dalton, rendered with warm flesh tones, rim lighting, and a contemplative, hardened gaze. Behind him in mid-ground profile, a secondary shirtless figure demonstrates a focused martial arts stance, establishing the protagonist's kinetic discipline. 

The base of the composition anchors the narrative setting with an architectural rendering of the "Double Deuce" roadside tavern, complete with a crowd queuing beneath the entrance canopy. The artist skillfully uses luminous cyan colored pencil against a dark charcoal-textured ground to simulate the neon glow of the stylized title typography and the roadside venue signage.

works.title: The Lost Boys
works.description:
CAST & WORLD INDEX
Characters: Alan Frog (Historical/Cinematic), David Powers (Historical/Cinematic), Edgar Frog (Historical/Cinematic), Michael Emerson (Historical/Cinematic), Sam Emerson (Historical/Cinematic)
Items: Boardwalk Carousel, Ferris Wheel, Roller Coaster, Trenchcoat
Places: Santa Carla Boardwalk
Special abilities: Vampirism
works.critique:
The piece achieves substantial technical authority precisely through its deliberate mastery of wax crayon—a medium typically resistant to fine-art precision. The authored display typography at the lower center anchors the composition, rendered with clean, hard-edged lettering despite the blunt tool.

McGary surmounts the inherent limitations of wax binder through disciplined pressure modulation and optical color blending:
* **Material Control in Anatomy:** Achieving five distinct, recognizable portrait likenesses across small spatial footprints requires acute tip control, particularly in defining the subtle facial planes of the lower quartet and David's brooding brow line.
* **Atmospheric & Background Detail:** The roller coaster scaffolding, Ferris wheel spokes, and carousel framing are executed with consistent line weight and spatial depth without smearing adjacent high-value zones.
* **Chromatic Transitioning:** The lower tier transitions seamlessly across distinct chromatic zones (red, yellow, blue, and green) without devolving into muddy brown buildup, demonstrating deliberate layer sequencing.

works.title: NOTHING TO SEE
works.critique: The line drawing in image_6d5f9f.jpg stands as a precise study of human forearms and hands engaged in an intense, localized action, serving as the core evaluation for Anatomical/Compositional Mastery. The draftsmanship utilizes clean, unshaded contour lines to establish the weight and posture of the gripping appendages. One hand is balled into a semi-fist, while the lower hand tightly grasps a loose fold of fabric or a structural band, creating an intersecting diagonal movement across the frame. The spatial layout intentionally strips away the rest of the body to force absolute focus onto the hands. This composition is driven by two isolated, heavily saturated red oval marks situated precisely over the wrists or carpal regions. These crimson focal points pierce the negative space, recontextualizing a simple anatomical sketch into a stark statement of wounding or marking.

works.title: TUMMY ACHE
works.critique:
The visual artifact found in image_475bab.jpg presents a concentrated iconographic study centered entirely within a stark white digital void. The core subject is a single, continuous spiral or vortex structure that funnels downward. Compositionally, the object transitions from expansive, loosely overlapping horizontal bands at its peak into an increasingly tight, vertical chain of bead-like segments at its root.

Anatomically and structurally, the piece strips away environmental context to investigate pure symbolic form. Radiating outward from the upper loop are five distinct, high-contrast energetic hash marks or crown spokes. These peripheral vectors introduce a directional illumination or explosive release effect, transforming a simple geometric coil into an active emblem of cognitive friction or generative power. The raw ink weight is variable, emphasizing a rapid, gestural execution that values thematic immediacy over polished commercial rendering.

works.title: WHAT DO YOU FEEL ABOUT IT DIGITAL INK
Learning Curve
works.critique: The drawing in image_6d7267.jpg uses a sequential schematic layout to map out a failed trajectory of flight or descent. Positioned around the core constraint of Anatomical/Compositional Mastery, the artist dispenses with traditional anatomical rendering to focus entirely on kinetic posture, spatial weight, and center of gravity. The composition relies on the stark contrast between the black ink figures and the red dotted tracking lines that signify intent versus execution. The narrative arc moves from a high precipice down through an interrupted parachute deployment, an impact event rendered with aggressive red marks, and a slow, stumbling post-impact crawl. The compositional flow forces the eye down an asymmetric diagonal axis, effectively using negative space to emphasize the isolation and scale of the fall.

works.title: SIBERIAN SF
works.critique:
The graphic composition in image_475046.jpg operates as an insulated study in architectural containment and stylized figuration. Encapsulated within a thick, rigid circular boundary, the subject is rendered from a three-quarter perspective, facing toward the left quadrant. The figure is clad in a mottled, textured cold-weather hazard or tactical suit that suggests extreme environmental conditions. The facial features are completely anonymized behind tinted protective goggles and a dark, heavy respiratory face mask, reinforcing a theme of severe personal alienation and survival under hostile circumstances.

Compositionally, the piece leverages strong spatial counterweights. The left hand holds a small, mechanical star-like gear or device close to the chest, while the right hand projects forward, holding a boxy, compact handheld transceiver or tactical tool. These foreground elements frame the torso, drawing focus upward to the hidden gaze of the operator. The backdrop features a vibrant, flat field of saturated crimson, interrupted by dripping, organic dark shapes that rise like a distant, burning skyline or suggest biochemical contamination. The contrast between the clinical white geometry of the suit and the fluid, chaotic background accents the tense equilibrium of the scene.

works.title: GRACE
works.critique:
The visual matrix of image_473d7b.jpg maps an evocative, allegorical narrative centered on existential survival and cognitive grounding. The primary subject—a figure with short dark hair and glasses—is captured in an attitude of exhaustion or deep contemplative repose, leaning heavily over a massive, open book that acts as a makeshift flotation device. Compositionally, the text blocks and the figure's upper torso remain buoyant above a field of loose, light blue digital washes representing water, while the legs extend downward, partially obscured and suspended within the fluid medium. A single red ribbon or bookmark spills from the center of the open text, cutting a sharp vertical line through the muted palette.

Anatomically and symbolically, the background elements contextualize this state of suspension as the aftermath of a macrocosmic disruption. Behind the floating figure, a dark gray storm cloud blankets the upper horizon. Looming within this shadow are the jagged remnants of a shipwreck or broken architecture, including a shattered, tilting wooden ladder and sharp, triangular peaks that mimic shark fins or submerged wreckage. The juxtaposition of these destructive elements against the stable, buoyant text block establishes a profound structural metaphor: the written word, canonical framework, or foundational code serves as the sole mechanism preventing total immersion in an overwhelming environment.

works.critique: The digital rendering in image_6cf9c6.jpg stands as a high-intensity exploration of portraiture, specifically evaluated under the rubric of Anatomical/Compositional Mastery. The composition utilizes an aggressive, tightly cropped frontal view that eliminates environmental context to prioritize facial topography. Anatomically, the underlying cranial structure is defined through harsh, high-contrast values, modeling the brow, nose bridge, and firm jawline using a restricted crimson palette against deep negative space. The glasses act as a critical compositional horizontal axis, intersecting the vertical alignment of the features and framing the eyes, which feature meticulous, sharp light reflections. The expressive, loose linework defining the hair adds kinetic energy to the upper perimeter, contrasting directly with the solid, immovable posture of the face.

works.critique:
The visual artifact designated as image_3d4c7a.jpg operates as a diagnostic psychodrama mapped across a rigid, downward-pointing structural vector. Compositionally, the piece utilizes an infographic or tracking chart layout to illustrate human deterioration. A large diagonal arrow slices down from the upper right to the lower left, broken into color-coded tiers that represent chronological stages of systemic or behavioral collapse.

At each level of the descent, simple geometric faces act as anatomical avatars for the mind's current state. The journey begins outside the arrow with an aggressive, determined countenance declaring, "LET'S DO THIS!!". As the boundary into "EMOTIONAL RELAPSE" is breached, the canvas shifts to a vibrant green field where the face reflects immediate exhaustion and defeat. The transition into "MENTAL RELAPSE" moves through a warm orange segment where nostalgia acts as an intellectual rationalization. The descent accelerates into "PHYSICAL RELAPSE," rendered in deep crimson, where cross-eyed intoxication signals a loss of bodily control. Finally, the path reaches "TOTAL RELAPSE" in a dark gray terminal zone, marked by slurred, orthographically fractured dialogue ("NIM NNOTT DRUHNNK..."), terminating at a foundational skull and crossbones icon at the arrow's tip. The layout effectively pairs structural design with psychological analysis, transforming abstract internal variables into a highly scannable visual warning system.

works.critique: The composition establishes balance between organic geological structures and gentle aquatic movement. Dark, jagged lava rock outcroppings anchor the foreground and midground, creating a natural frame that pulls the viewer's eye across the translucent green waters of the lagoon toward the lush tropical canopy along the shoreline. The artist uses loose, expressive gestures for the palm foliage and trees, relying on layered watercolor-style washes of sage, olive, and cyan to render depth, reflections, and tropical atmosphere.

works.title: APART
works.critique:
The visual array presented in image_3d5f1c.png relies on absolute negative space to articulate its core thematic argument. Positioned horizontally across the longitudinal axis of a blank white void, two disembodied human hands reach toward one another but are permanently arrested before making contact. The structural tension of the piece dictates that the empty space between the fingertips functions as the true focal point, transforming a simple study of extremities into a stark monument to structural isolation and fractured dialogue.

Anatomically, the artist executes the forms via a rapid, high-contrast digital ink outline with zero interior shading or texture. The hand on the left is scaled smaller, suggesting either an organic structural discrepancy, a forced perspective depth, or an inherent imbalance in agency. Its fingers are outstretched but tightly grouped, with a sharply defined thumb pointing down into the lower quadrant. The right hand mirrors this trajectory with larger, more expressive scaling, its fingers slightly separated as if straining against the invisible barrier dividing them. The deliberate simplicity of the contours emphasizes a raw, symbolic shorthand that communicates the somatic memory of reaching out rather than an interest in academic hand modeling.

works.title: CAN I MOVE YOU?
works.critique:
The visual architecture of image_4754de.jpg centers on a stark dialogic tension between two human entities captured within an unrendered void. The composition features a dual representation of subjects operating on distinct spatial planes. The upper, standing figure is rendered in a minimalist, high-contrast block of dark ink for the torso and legs, wearing distinct rectangular glasses and staring forward with a neutral, slightly geometric countenance. In his left hand, he loosely trail-holds an electrical cord or plug, serving as a subtle mechanical metaphor for connection, power, or disruption.

Positioned lower in the frame and oriented along a sharp diagonal vector is a reclining figure, whose upward gaze directly meets the vertical figure's presence. This prone subject features a defined jawline, short cropped hair, and a distinct beard, captured in a state of alert repose or sudden interruption. Dividing these two figures is the heavily stylized, jaggedly brushed textual inquiry: "CAN I MOVE YOU?" The text does not merely label the canvas; it functions as a visual barrier and a psychological bridge between the passive, resting subject and the active, standing observer. The anatomical mastery is deliberate in its rough shorthand, prioritizing kinetic weight and emotional posture over precise academic formalisms.

works.title: DRAG ME TO HELL
works.critique: The composition employs a classic theatrical poster hierarchy, placing a towering, sinister visage in the background to loom over a struggling, foreshortened victim in the lower foreground. The contrast between deep black shadows, fiery orange/yellow highlights, and pale flesh tones reinforces a sense of impending doom. Sharp, expressive line work outlines facial features and frantic gestures, while stylized typography anchors the base to complete the poster layout.

works.title: FRONT SLEEP
works.critique:
The visual work in image_48bce5.jpg centers on a prone human figure rendered in a state of deep exhaustion, rest, or withdrawal. The structural composition is defined by a bold, foreshortened perspective that angles the viewer's eye from the crown of the head down to the upturned feet. The subject is confined entirely to a gray, padded rectangular mat or air mattress floating within a blank white void, which intensifies the thematic weight of isolation and psychological containment.

Anatomically, the artist wrestles with complex spatial overlap. The head is completely obscured by a stark white pillow, which acts as a visual shield against the outside world. The arms are tucked defensively underneath the torso and pillow, with only the forearms and wrists visible. The body is draped in black garments accented by a singular, high-contrast red stripe running down the outer leg, creating a strong diagonal vector that guides the eye through the length of the pose. The feet are splayed outward at the base of the frame, rendered with minimal line work that favors functional gestural shorthand over rigorous anatomical accuracy.

works.title: UNTITLED GUITARMAN SILHOUETTE
works.critique:
The graphic composition in image_3d5493.jpg presents a high-contrast exploration of performance energy, utilizing a stark black silhouette floating within an unrendered white void. The core subject is a single human figure locked in an aggressive, wide-stance musical posture while handling an electric stringed instrument or guitar. By stripping away all interior anatomical indicators, facial expressions, or vestigial details, the artist forces the viewer to focus entirely on the outer contour lines, tracking the kinetic momentum of the pose.

Anatomically and structurally, the silhouette establishes an energetic diagonal axis. The head is tilted downward toward the neck of the instrument, while the knees are bent in a stabilizing, athletic crouch. Extending directly below the feet is a prominent, low-frequency gray ground shadow. Rather than mirroring the silhouette symmetrically, this shadow is dramatically elongated and skewed forward along a counter-diagonal vector. This spatial displacement between the solid black entity and its fluid gray projection creates a powerful illusion of volumetric depth and stage illumination, heightening the thematic weight of a performance captured mid-cadence.

works.title: ONLY JOSH IN THE BUILDING
works.critique: The composition uses structural architecture as a focal boundary, embedding the central subject within a double-hung window frame that acts as a natural lens. The subject's reflective pose—holding a notebook and pen while gazing outward—evokes introspective contemplation and observation. Dynamic contrast is achieved through bold black shirt fills against grayscale interior tones, balanced by the strong geometric lines of the exterior window sill and trim.

works.title: NOTHING TO SAY
works.critique: The illustration in image_6d6366.jpg provides a compelling study in narrative contrast, evaluated under the rubric of Anatomical/Compositional Mastery. The central figure is rendered with heavy, expressive cross-hatching and ink washes that articulate a solid, grounded physical posture. The proportions are slightly stylized but structurally sound, capturing a weary, weighted stance as the figure holds an acoustic guitar by the neck in one hand and clutches a composition notebook under the opposite arm. Compositionally, the density of the figures—clothed in dark garments and a detailed Batman shirt—is sharply interrupted by a thick, bright red speech bubble. This bubble contains absolutely no text or interior linework, creating an intentional, jarring focal point of negative space that pulls the eye directly away from the physical form to highlight an absence.

works.title: A HERO IN ALL OF US
LOVE MANKIND SINNER REPENT
works.critique:
The multi-figured narrative array in image_47b27c.jpg constructs a dense psychological tableau. Positioned beneath the dripping, high-contrast crimson phrase "LOVE MANKIND SINNER REPENT," four distinct figures interact in an unfolding sequence of mania, enforcement, and despair. Compositionally, the vector of action flows laterally, anchoring a complex ideological conflict into specific character gestures.

Anatomically and structurally, each entity embodies a specific behavioral archetype. On the far left, a figure enclosed in a bright red protective hazardous materials suit and mesh mask extends a sterile, mechanical hand toward a seated man in a gold tunic, while holding an instrument or scanner. The seated figure is locked in a state of hysterical, open-mouthed laughter, completely detached from the reality of his confinement or evaluation. To his right, an athletic, shirtless figure stands aggressively with hands raised in a dual gesture of warning and brandished force, raising a fencing foil aloft. This blade drips with red ink, pointing directly toward the final figure on the right—a man in a blue tunic covering his face in absolute grief or weeping isolation. The stark contrast between the bright, flat color blocks and the sketchy, immediate line work emphasizes the underlying themes of psychological fracturing and institutional pressure.

works.title: XIV
works.critique: The illustration in image_6d6b42.jpg demonstrates a strong mastery of high-contrast ink composition and graphic framing. Evaluating the piece on Anatomical/Compositional Mastery, the artist employs bold, expressive black fills to isolate the two central figures, grounding their forward stride while creating an asymmetrical, heavy shadow in the lower right foreground. The stylized anatomy captures naturalistic kinetic movement—the interlinked arms, the tilt of the heads, and a casual mid-walk gesture—rendered with clean, confident outlines. Behind the figures, the compositional depth is managed via a textured shop window display. This background layer utilizes high-contrast negative shapes and finer linework to render a complex scene within a scene, drawing the viewer's eye through a sequence of internal frames.

works.critique:
The visual composition in image_491318.jpg operates as a multi-layered text-and-image landscape, structured around a central framed window. The dominant focal point is the bold, blue-shaded block lettering "LET GO LOVE," which physically cuts across and obscures an underlying manuscript of handwritten musical lyrics and guitar chords (D, G, A). This deliberate layering forces the viewer to parse the piece chronologically, peeling back the overarching directive to read the vulnerable, questioning narrative trapped beneath it.

Anatomically and compositionally, the peripheral figures serve as symbolic allegories for the text's central tension between holding on and releasing control. In the bottom-left corner, a small, stylized self-portrait figure stands in profile, holding scissors in one hand while grasping a cluster of hanging strings or wires in the other. This figure anchors the lower boundary and directs its gaze upward toward the floating balloons. At the center base, a pair of open, upturned hands are rendered symmetrically, a universal motif for surrender or letting go. The upper border is bracketed by simplistic clouds and three ascending balloons, which offer a literal and whimsical manifestation of the title's command, contrasting sharply with the grounded, dark-clothed figure below.

works.critique:
The visual artwork in image_47ba1c.jpg showcases a dynamic dual performance, effectively merging graphic illustration with a poster-like structural frame. The foreground figure, clearly identifiable by a prominent high-contrast Batman insignia on his chest shirt, anchors the right side of the composition. He is captured mid-performance, handling an acoustic guitar with an expressive, wide-mouthed vocal stance. The anatomical execution utilizes bold black inks and heavy shading on the clothing, establishing a powerful low-frequency weight that contrasts with the lighter, more agile lines of the secondary performer.

Behind him, a keyboardist injects a sense of erratic, high-energy movement into the scene. Her pose is dramatically elongated, with red-streaked hair thrown back, heart-shaped glasses, and a tongue-out gesture that indicates a raw, unrefined musical environment. The keyboard is angled sharply across the lower-left quadrant, creating a strong diagonal vector that guides the viewer's eye up through the performance space. A subtle yet significant symbol—a small pink broken heart—is placed on the body of the guitar, offering a hidden emotional counterpoint to the energetic, public nature of the presentation. Overhead, the stylized "TTO" monogram incorporates a crackling lightbulb graphic, serving as an emblem of immediate, raw inspiration.

works.title: WHAT ARE LITTLE GIRLS MADE OF
WAKANDA FOREVER
works.critique:
The artwork employs a stark chiaroscuro graphic style, using heavy black ink fills to carve out two figures positioned back-to-back against a dense, textured black background field. Compositionally, the layout contrasts organic human facial topography on the left against sleek, masked metallic armor on the right, establishing a strong structural duality across the horizontal axis.

In terms of Anatomical and Compositional Mastery (Expertise: 6.8), the artist utilizes bold hatching and localized color accents—specifically vibrant gold lining across the shoulders and mask trim, subtle blue highlights along the collar, and a vivid green earring detail—to model volume and light direction. The anatomical proportions capture intense facial tension in the unmasked figure, while the adjoining masked profile establishes a protective, vigilant counter-pose. The heavy ink boundaries ground the dual subject matter securely within the central frame, utilizing negative space effectively to define peripheral contours.

works.title: GIO
works.critique: The portrait features an exaggerated caricature style characterized by a disproportionately large head, distinct thick-rimmed glasses, and expressive facial cross-hatching. The central figure holds a small device against a interior architectural backdrop framed by brickwork and hanging lighting fixtures. High-contrast dark inks ground the figure's clothing, while soft gray brushwork serves as a vignetting background layer to focus visual weight directly onto the subject's gaze.

works.title: BOSTON LEGAL
works.critique: The drawing features two suited figures rendered in a stylized caricature aesthetic, each holding a cigar. The linework relies on clean, black ink contours with sharp variations in line weight to define tailoring, facial structure, and expressive gestures. Anatomically, the proportions compress the body shapes while expanding head scale and facial nuances, highlighting distinctive expressions of calm confidence and casual poise. The monogram initials "BL" rest at the bottom center, anchoring the duo within a balanced visual frame.

works.title: SISTERS & MISTERS
works.critique: The graphic composition presents four stylized character heads arranged in a quad formation against a textured red knit sweater backdrop. The portraits deliberately omit central facial features such as noses and mouths while retaining expressive eyebrows, distinctive hairstyles, and vivid eyes, evoking a minimalist yet iconic aesthetic reminiscent of vintage mid-century illustration and holiday iconography. Surrounding white embroidered-style snowflakes act as framing elements, while clean white serif typography at the base anchors the visual title. The juxtaposition of smooth digital vector-like linework against the tactile background creates an engaging visual warmth.

works.text:

works.critique:
"Layers" operates as an astute, witty deconstruction of contemporary digital draftsmanship. By pulling the 2D digital workspace into axonometric three-dimensional physical space, McGary literalizes the invisible mechanics of the artist's stack: floating raster planes, alpha channels, bounding boxes, and the familiar hierarchy of the digital layer inspector (with "Layer 26", "Layer 25", and "Layer 22" visible). 

The authored title "Layers" functions with deliberate dual meaning: it identifies both the core technical paradigm of digital image creation and the philosophical, self-reflective layers of the artist inspecting an emerging self-image. The artist stands in contemplative scrutiny—hand to chin, gesturing with an open measuring hand—directly confronting the transparent strata of his own anatomical construction. 

Compositionally, the piece relies on a strong diagonal thrust moving from upper right to lower left, balanced by the solid, weighted black silhouette of the standing figure against the transparent, floating glass-like canvases. The line work balances loose, energetic ink hatching on the physical body with clean, drafted wireframes on the floating interfaces, demonstrating both expressive figurative draftsmanship and controlled linear perspective.

works.title: ONE OF OUR PLANETS IS MISSING
works.text:
42.64
1.14.23
ONE OF OUR PLANETS IS MISSING
works.critique: The graphic illustration relies on high-contrast black-and-white ink rendering, starkly set against a solid cyan background. Foreshortening plays a key role in the compositional weight, pushing the subject's boots and raised hands into dramatic perspective relative to the seated figure. Stylized, sharp typography is stacked vertically on the right flank, balancing the expressive gesture of the central figure with rigid geometric structure. Heavy black fills and energetic cross-hatching define shadow and form, lending an intense, dramatic energy to the scene.

works.title: ONE OF OUR PLANETS IS MISSING
RUDY
works.critique:
The artwork employs a compressed, stylized caricature style to stage a direct visual parody of the iconic Notre Dame "Fighting Irish" mascot logo. By mapping the famous crouched, fists-up combat stance of the leprechaun onto a football player clutching a gridiron ball to his chest, the composition achieves an immediate thematic synthesis between collegiate athletic mythology and cinematic pop-culture folklore (*Rudy*).

In terms of Anatomical and Compositional Mastery (Expertise: 5.5), the drawing deliberately mirrors the wide, angular leg stance and raised upper-body silhouette of the classic emblem. Thick, high-contrast black ink outlines establish clean graphic boundaries, filled with flat color blocks of gold, blue, gray, and dark brown. The bold varsity-letter "R" positioned below functions as a graphic pedestal, anchoring the dynamic lateral posture of the figure and balancing the exaggerated head-to-body proportion.

works.title: The Spectre
works.critique: The work employs a stylized, chibified figure rendering executed with bold ink contours, precise cross-hatching, and halftone shading overlays. The composition is grounded by custom typography on the left and a muted, aged parchment background texture that enhances the classic pop-art aesthetic. Anatomically, the proportions are intentionally squatted to emphasize character expression and costume silhouettes, particularly the exaggerated green cowl and cape framing the shadow-draped face.

works.title: ICY ROAD
works.critique:
The artwork presents a humorous, graphic subversion of standard regulatory road signage. Rather than featuring the typical skidding automobile icon on the yellow diamond warning sign, the composition replaces the vehicle with a small silhouette figure navigating squiggly traction marks. On close inspection, the silhouette bears the distinct profile of glasses and a prominent yellow Batman chest emblem, directly linking the icon to JOSH MCGARY's established self-portrait archetype.

Compositionally (Expertise: 6.2), the drawing relies on crisp geometric symmetry balanced against an unrendered white background. The bright yellow diamond and rectangular "ICY ROAD" sign are anchored to a central dark post rooted in a sketched patch of snow and ice. The clean line work and bold primary colors reflect a pop-art, graphic design sensibility that effectively converts personal daily experience into a universal warning symbol for precarious navigation and unstable ground.

works.title: GORN
works.critique: The figure depicts a reptilian humanoid warrior rendered in full-body stance, wielding a dark dagger in its right hand. The drawing employs distinct, clean black outlines combined with muted green, brown, and tan flat color fills. Anatomically, the posture captures a wide, dynamic stance, emphasizing heavy limbs and clawed feet. Special attention is given to the segmented, grid-patterned chest armor and the stylized textured head, complete with sharp, interlocking teeth and compound eye details.

works.title: MAGICALLY THEY'RE VICIOUS
works.critique:
The graphic artwork executes an explicit pop-culture confrontation enclosed within a circular emblem frame. Compositionally, the piece stages a direct clash between two opposing cultural interpretations of the same folklore archetype: Lucky the Leprechaun (the iconic Lucky Charms breakfast cereal mascot) leaping cheerfully in the foreground, contrasted against Lubdan (the gnarled, predatory antagonist from the *Leprechaun* horror film series) looming directly behind him.

In terms of Anatomical and Compositional Mastery (Expertise: 6.5), the drawing relies on a stark dichotomy of illustrative styles. The foreground mascot is rendered in a flat, clean-lined, mid-century commercial cartoon aesthetic, complete with his signature green coat, marshmallow-sparking clover wand, and joyful expression. In direct opposition, the horror-movie leprechaun in the background is rendered with textured chiaroscuro shading, gnarled claws, sharp teeth, and sinister, deeply creased facial anatomy. The vibrant rainbow arc background serves as both a literal reference to the cereal's legendary marketing motif and a graphic framing device that holds the two opposing figures in dynamic visual tension.

works.title: RED ROBIN
works.critique:
The piece presents a witty literalization of the commercial brand name "Red Robin" by merging the restaurant chain's familiar typography with the DC Comics superhero Red Robin (Tim Drake). The character is depicted holding up a gourmet burger on a platter, stepping seamlessly into the role of brand mascot within the iconic yellow oval frame.

The title "RED ROBIN" functions both as a literal reading of the corporate logotype reproduced in the artwork and as a double entendre referencing the comic book hero. By juxtaposing fast-casual dining branding with superhero costuming, the work plays on visual familiarity, brand recognition, and pop-culture mashup humor. The draftsmanship is clean, vibrant, and confident, executing the graphic logo style and cartoon illustration with precise line work and bold primary colors.

works.title: GOING HOME
works.critique: The piece utilizes loose, gestural linework combined with flat color fills to illustrate a drone navigating past a stylized tree canopy. Motion lines project dynamically behind the quadcopter, emphasizing rapid directional flight, while a speech bubble containing a house icon anchors the narrative theme of automated return or homing routines. Compositionally, the focal point is balanced between the stark mechanical entity and the organic foliage, creating a clear visual contrast between technology and natural landscape elements.

works.title: FIRST WORSHIP
works.critique:
The drawing features two figures seated side-by-side on outdoor wooden porch steps, engaged in a passionate acoustic music jam and worship session. The figure on the right is a self-portrait representation of JOSH MCGARY—characterized by a athletic stance, short dark hair, and a dark shirt—strumming a large acoustic guitar with a wide-mouthed, vocal delivery. Beside him, a second figure leans back with head upturned, holding a smaller stringed instrument while singing in unison.

Compositionally (Expertise: 6.5), the piece employs gestural black ink linework with heavy fill blocks on the clothing and guitar body. Floating musical notes surround both performers, while a prominent, speech-style thought bubble containing a Latin cross originates directly between their heads. This symbolic placement anchors the acoustic performance to a shared spiritual foundation, illustrating how musical labor transforms domestic space into an altar of worship.

works.title: FOR SHURE!
works.critique: The drawing employs a stark, minimalist black-and-white line style to depict a dynamic interaction between two stylized figures. The figure on the left, displaying exaggerated vocal expression and pointing emphatically, holds up a garment next to a discarded pile on the floor. A speech bubble declaring "THIS TIME FOR SHURE!" drives the comedic tone, while the skeptical posture of the second figure on the right provides visual contrast and narrative weight. Compositionally, negative space dominates, focusing complete attention on the expressive posturing and gesture of the subjects.

works.title: OFFICE
works.critique: The architectural layout of the home office/entertainment hub reflects an organized system of media consumption and creative inspiration. The central focus—the monitor flanked by framed posters and surrounded by curated shelves of physical media—establishes an archetype of modern digital and physical curation. The line work relies on minimalist contouring, utilizing simple geometry to construct perspective and depth within a confined interior environment. Color accents in soft yellow and subtle cyan act as lighting highlights, guiding the viewer's eye across the ceiling lights and display cases.

works.title: NO RETURN
works.critique: The illustration features a stylized self-portrait of a figure trapped behind and pinned by a giant hourglass. The composition uses foreshortening on the figure's forward-reaching hands to establish immediate depth, driving focus toward the strained, anxious expression of the subject. Soft flesh tones and light yellow sand hues contrast with sharp, gestural black ink outlines. The glass vessel serves as both a literal obstruction and a metaphorical clamp, emphasizing the physical weight of passing time.

works.title: COFFIN DOORWAY
works.critique: The illustration features a stylized figure emerging dramatically from an open casket in a graveyard setting, wearing sunglasses with bright red lenses, a Batman logo shirt, and holding a red electric guitar. The dynamic forward reach of the central figure creates immediate depth and narrative tension against the standing silhouette of a woman viewed from behind. Line work is loose yet confident, utilizing high-contrast black ink, gray shading on the casket structure, and focal pops of vibrant red pigment to draw direct focus to the figure's face and instrument.

works.title: BACKED UP
works.critique: The composition employs a schematic layout to depict a dual-source convergence system encountering a critical blockage. Two structures labeled 'B' and 'L' route fluid directional vectors—signified by blue and brown arrows—toward a central collection reservoir. The primary tension point is highlighted by a red negation symbol and an exclamation mark, indicating a system overflow or backup originating from the left node. Visually, the clear separation of lines and targeted use of primary accent colors prioritize functional diagrammatic logic over formal illusionism.

works.title: OPTIONS
works.critique: The drawing features a solitary figure rendered from behind, facing two closed doors labeled "BAD" and "WORSE." A thought bubble above the figure displays a complex, insoluble mathematical equation, emphasizing the cognitive strain of weighing non-ideal outcomes. In his left hand, lowered at his side, the figure holds a firearm, introducing an element of underlying crisis or tactical defense. The monochromatic tone, broken only by subtle yellow accents on the door handles, highlights the stark, binary nature of the forced choice.

works.critique:
The sheet functions as an analytical character design document, breaking down facial anatomy, specific ethnic features ("Italian nose"), prop callouts, and costume variants into a coherent visual taxonomy. The composition balances loose, searching gestural studies with precise schematic callouts (the choker mechanism, mask design, and elemental generator cuff).

The cyan digital line work maintains consistent energy across varied perspectives—from profile turns to emotive headshots and full-body wardrobe configurations. The interplay of technical hero gear (modified firefighter turnouts, power cuffs) with civilian/ironic elements ("Smokey the Bear shirt") adds depth and practical worldbuilding logic to the character's functional visual identity.

works.title: TURD GOBLIN-295
works.critique:
JOSH MCGARY constructs the drawing around a descending chain of attention. Four uncertain observers occupy the upper field, a central figure bends over an open toilet, and a grotesque creature receives or consumes the toilet’s contents below. The eye therefore travels from collective bewilderment to private action and finally to embodied appetite. This vertical arrangement gives the sketch more compositional intelligence than its casual linework initially suggests.

The question marks are not merely indicators of confusion. Repeated above separate heads, they establish uncertainty as a shared social condition. The witnesses see the act but possess no interpretive framework adequate to it. Their presence transforms the image from an isolated absurdity into a study of spectatorship: the grotesque becomes possible within a community that observes, wonders, and nevertheless remains passive.

The central human figure supplies the work’s crucial ambiguity. The posture may indicate feeding, disposal, discovery, or participation. Because the hand and toilet-plunger-like form are only loosely resolved, the exact action remains unstable. That instability is thematically productive, even where it reflects limited anatomical clarity. The figure mediates between civilized sanitation and monstrous consumption, turning the toilet from an instrument of removal into an altar or feeding station.

The creature is drawn with the greatest graphic certainty. Its narrowed eye, horn-like projections, distended mouth, and triangular teeth compress appetite, hostility, and satisfaction into a blunt emblem. The visible waste above its face makes the metaphor deliberately indecorous: what ordinary life attempts to expel can become nourishment for a malformed appetite. The vulgarity is functional rather than incidental.

Anatomical and compositional mastery receives 6.2. The figures are recognizable, gestures communicate, silhouettes remain distinct, and the descending focal structure is effective. However, several bodies lack convincing volume, the central hand-and-tool relationship is unclear, spatial depth is largely symbolic, and some contours terminate without structural resolution. The large empty field also makes the group feel suspended rather than situated. Even so, the asymmetrical placement of the goblin counterbalances the human cluster and prevents the page from becoming inert.

The strongest quality is conceptual economy. A few spectators, a toilet, and a voracious monster produce a complete moral ecosystem: bewildered observation above, ambiguous human mediation in the center, and undisguised consumption below. The drawing does not merely portray something disgusting. It asks what happens when expelled corruption acquires an audience, a servant, and an appetite.

works.title: Self Portrait
works.critique: The piece utilizes a circular, vignette-like frame to anchor a frontal portrait, employing high-contrast black line art against warm, saturated orange and skin-tone palettes. The integrate of screen-tone patterns (halftone dots and diagonal hatching) pays homage to vintage comic book printing techniques. Anatomically, the facial structure is deliberate and stylized, emphasizing intense eye contact behind thick-rimmed glasses and a furrowed brow, projecting stoic determination and concentration.

works.title: BRIT AND THE WHALE
works.critique:
The drawing presents an intimate study of observational portraiture, focusing on a figure leaning forward in concentrated creative work. Compositionally, the artwork creates a compelling "art-within-art" meta-narrative: the subject is depicted actively painting or rendering a cetacean form (a whale surrounded by blue water washes) within a spiral-bound notebook resting on a desk surface.

Anatomically and structurally (Expertise: 6.2), the piece relies on loose, expressive contour line work with targeted soft color fills. The posture conveys a realistic kinetic sense of quiet focus—the curvature of the spine, the angle of the head, and the deliberate grip on the thin brush. The selective application of color (warm blonde hair tones, a single gold pendant accent, and the aquatic blue field on the notebook page) focuses visual gravity directly on the point of artistic creation. The isolated white background isolates the subject and desk, stripping away environmental distraction to prioritize the act of focused rendering.

works.title: DAY THREE
works.critique: The drawing uses minimalist, quick contour line art to portray a figure leaning forward while working on a laptop. The subject's slouched posture and focused head angle create a sense of deep immersion and solitary study. Floating above the figure, a cloud-like thought bubble containing a Latin cross establishes a distinct conceptual focal point, contrasting the physical reality of screen-based labor with internal, faith-based or theological rumination. The composition effectively balances open negative space with concentrated linework around the subject's face, hands, and device.

works.title: CITY ON THE EDGE OF FOREVER
Primal Fear
works.critique: The work employs minimalist line art to probe themes of identity, social masking, and latent vulnerability. Visual tension is established by placing a placid, handheld mask over the subject's face while furrowed brows remain exposed behind it. Compositionally, the stark economy of line eliminates extraneous detail to center entirely on the dynamic between public presentation and internal distress.

works.title: PORTO MONTIZ MADEIRA, PORTUGAL DIGITAL INK
CATHETER PANTS
works.text:
43.27 / SKETCHES / 12.4.23 PM
WE CAN DO IT
works.critique:
The piece is an autobiographical single-panel gag cartoon exploring the absurdities of idiosyncratic DIY product design. The provisional title "CATHETER PANTS -29" directly states the invention concept, which is humorously framed inside the drawing by the creator's determined pitch: "WE CAN DO IT".

Compositionally, the piece is arranged in a classic two-point narrative layout:
* **The Pitch / Inventor:** Positioned on the right in profile, the artist renders himself with thick-rimmed glasses, a goatee, and casual studio clothes, holding up a physical garment prototype while gesturing toward the blackboard like an earnest patent inventor.
* **The Schematic Blackboard:** Dominating the left field, the dark board features negative white-line schematics detailing overalls/suspender pants, internal drainage tubing, fluid bags, and pocket housing dimensions.
* **Environmental Accents:** The mesh wastebasket and low wall electrical outlet anchor the scene in a grounded domestic or workshop interior.

The inking style is clean, spontaneous, and economical, utilizing high-contrast solid black fills in the clothing and chalkboard backdrop to create strong negative-space readability.

works.title: COUNCIL OF JOSH
works.critique:
"COUNCIL OF JOSH" serves as a recursive amphitheater of the psyche, staging an overwhelming confrontation between an upward-looking ego and an amphitheater filled with its own fragmented personas. The composition is built on a steep, theatrical low-angle perspective: the extreme foreground features the crown and upturned gaze of the subject, pinned beneath the collective weight of dozens of internal archetypes leaning over a viewing parapet.

The tiered assembly operates as a visual inventory of cognitive states, past eras, anxieties, and aesthetic styles. The artist ranges from simplified anime and minimalist cartoon caricatures on the periphery to fully hatched, volumetric portraits in the central ring. Prominently seated at the center of the inner council is an incarnation bearing a bright red clown nose—a potent symbol of self-deprecation and performative vulnerability flanked by hyper-critical, exasperated, analytical, and manic iterations. Batman iconography recurs across multiple shirts, reinforcing an internal mythology of brooding vigilance juxtaposed with comedic absurdity.

The color economy is deliberate: stark monochrome linework recedes into deep shadow at the top, allowing the saturated ochre skin tones in the foreground, the glowing yellow chest insignia, and the singular red clown nose to anchor the narrative triangle. The work functions as both a celebration of milestone entry 200 and a forensic dissection of hyper-metacognitive self-surveillance.

The expressive, open-mouthed facial expression and exaggerated quill gesture introduce an element of self-aware theatricality, juxtaposing the traditional, archaic tool of classical literature against a modern comic-book graphic aesthetic.

works.critique:
The track "Our Secret" functions as a core compositional unit within the album project *A Lovesick Lament*. Framed within a concise duration of 2 minutes and 14 seconds, the arrangement prioritizes sonic economy and architectural clarity over ornamental padding.

In terms of Arrangement & Sonic Architecture (Expertise: 7.5), the piece employs a tightly integrated indie/alternative framework. The structural dynamics build around focused vocal delivery paired with rhythmic and melodic counterpoints, establishing an intimate yet resonant acoustic environment. The melodic phrasing reflects balanced cleverness and structural intent, maintaining thematic coherence across its concise runtime.
